title: Sakura Shōten customer restroom: sanitary ware
source: Original Johansson Town design, drawn in CAD (tools/cad/build-sakura-restroom-cad.py) and finished in Blender (tools/blender/build-sakura-restroom.py). Proportions follow ordinary 1990s Japanese close-coupled toilets with a hand-wash cistern lid and a pedestal basin with a single cold pillar tap; no maker's model is copied.
frame: Each fixture: wall plane at Y=0, the fixture stands out to +Y, X across (centred), Z up from the finished floor. Placed in the shop, the toilet's +X is north.

toilet.who: Customers of the shop and Thuan herself; the only public toilet on Main Street between the ferry and the park.
toilet.why: A close-coupled toilet with the hand-wash spout on its cistern lid: the refill water is used once to wash hands before it flushes, which is why a small shop room with a cold supply only has one.
toilet.where: Against the west wall, centred on the room's depth, so the door swing and the basin stay clear and the vent block is over the cistern.

lever.side: The north side of the tank, by the paper holder, where the hand already is; the supply and its stop valve come up on the south side, off the wall the basin shares.

washbasin.who: Everyone who has used the toilet, and Thuan rinsing the mop cloth.
washbasin.why: A pedestal basin hides its trap and needs no cupboard to rot in a damp room; one cold pillar tap because the shop has no hot water at the front.
washbasin.where: On the south wall under the mirror, beside the door, so hands are washed on the way out.

placement.note: Shop frame, metres (src/world/interiors/sakura-layout.js): x east, y up, z south to north.

decor.who: Thuan, who keeps the shop and cleans this room five times a day (the owner, 26 November 2026: "make the room more cute, remember a Japanese cute girl has decorated it").
decor.covers: Pink terry covers on the seat and the lid: a cold seat in a tiled room is the first thing a customer notices.
